blocks.text: Alkenes are prepared by removing small atoms (H, OH, X) from adjacent carbon atoms of saturated compounds so as to create a double bond; these are elimination reactions, in which a small molecule such as H2O or HCl is removed from adjacent carbons of an organic molecule. Ethene is prepared as follows.

Ethene is prepared by heating a mixture of ethanol and excess concentrated sulfuric acid at 180 degrees C; a water molecule is removed from the alcohol: CH3CH2OH with H2SO4 and heat gives CH2=CH2 + H2O. In the first step ethyl hydrogen sulfate is formed, CH3CH2OH + H2SO4 giving CH3CH2OSO3H + H2O, and it decomposes on heating to ethene: CH3CH2OSO3H gives CH2=CH2 + H2SO4.

On heating ethyl bromide with alcoholic KOH, ethene is formed; hydrogen and halogen are removed from adjacent carbons to create the double bond: CH3CH2Br + KOH (alcoholic) with heat gives CH2=CH2 + KBr + H2O.
Give the reactions of propanol with H2SO4 and the dehydrohalogenation of bromopropane.
